title: Counting, Symmetries and Equivalence Classes of Sudoku Grids
summary: Sudoku is a widely popular puzzle whose complete grids have been enumerated computationally: there are approximately $6.67 \times 10^{21}$ of them and, up to symmetry and renaming of digits, $5,472,730,538$ essentially different ones. The classical enumeration reduces the count to $44$ equivalence classes of the first band through a chain of ad hoc reductions, leaving the number $44$ without any apparent structural explanation.
